Doctor: Have you experienced any instability, locking, or difficulty bearing weight on the right knee since the injury?
Patient: I haven't had any real instability, but it's been pretty painful to put weight on it. I've been able to walk a little, but it's swollen and feels tight. I didn't really lock up or anything like that.
Doctor: Have you noticed any locking, clicking, or giving way of the knee? Have you been able to fully bend or straighten the knee?
Patient: I haven't noticed any locking or clicking, but I did feel a pop when it happened. As for bending or straightening, I can get through the full range of motion, but it feels tight and hurts a little when I do.
Doctor: Could you describe the exact mechanism of the injury, such as whether you twisted your knee, landed awkwardly, or collided with something while skiing?
Patient: Sure, I was skiing with some friends, and it was snowing pretty hard. I couldn't really see well, and the two paths kind of came together. I think the front end of my skis dug into the snow, and I ended up doing a cartwheel but kind of stopped halfway through. I could feel a pop in my right knee right then, and the pain came right after that.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays or MRI for your knee injury, and if so, what were the findings?
